A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same PS-Eval research work, including all main sections and Appendices A–P. Text comparison and matched page renderings establish complete, unchanged scientific content despite changes to publication headers, acknowledgments and reference pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAE experiments, including activation-function and layer comparisons in Sections 6–7, open SAE evaluations in Appendix K, and additional layer comparisons in Appendix O.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including Figures 3–6, the open SAE scores in Table 7, and the layer comparisons in Tables 10–13.

M1.justification: The PS-Eval input template and maximum-activation comparison procedure remain identical. SAE architectures, training losses and auxiliary-loss procedures in Section 3 and Appendices A/H are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same WiC-derived PS-Eval dataset and WiC/RedPajama training domains (Sections 3.2 and 4.1; Appendix B). No evaluated dataset, task, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparisons: LLM activations versus SAE features, ReLU versus TopK and JumpReLU variants, and sparse versus dense autoencoders (Section 6; Appendices E/J). Comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain 1,112 balanced evaluation examples (Table 1), the same training budgets, model configurations and metrics, and the same layer-4/layer-6 evaluation protocols in Appendix O.

E4.justification: The Ghost Grad ablation, training-domain comparison, dense-autoencoder analysis, expansion/activation/layer studies and logit-lens case studies are all retained unchanged, including their appendix evidence.

E5.justification: Figure 10 already describes error bars as variation across three seeds in v1, and v2 retains that caption and the same uncertainty displays. No run-count disclosure or statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical entries, plotted results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout. For example, Table 7 retains accuracies of 0.66, 0.51 and 0.52 for GPT-2 small, Pythia 70M and Gemma2-2B, respectively; Tables 10–13 also match exactly.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations remain unchanged, including the SAE losses, PS-Eval decision rules, activation-function definitions and random-SAE probability derivation in Appendix D.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: PS-Eval, the limits of MSE–L0 evaluation, and findings concerning latent dimensionality, deeper layers and attention. No scientific claim is strengthened or narrowed.

C2.justification: Section 8 retains the limitation that maximum activation may not represent the intended word meaning. Interpretations of layer/component results, cautions about specificity, and applicability discussions in Appendix P are also unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details and access information are unchanged, including Table 4's training configuration, auxiliary-loss settings, code/dataset links and Appendix K's pretrained-model links. The new funding acknowledgment adds no technical reproducibility information.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning are identical, including Section 2 and Appendix P. The reference list is repaginated without adding, removing or revising its cited content.

P1.justification: v2 replaces 'Preprint.' with 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2025' and adds an Acknowledgments section crediting HF's JSPS KAKENHI grant JP22J21582. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The acknowledgment and reference-spacing changes alter bibliography layout, placing the final reference on a separate page and shifting appendix pagination. Figures 1–20 and Tables 1–13 retain their displays, captions and arrangement.

improvement.justification: v2 adds funding attribution and updates publication presentation, but the methods, evidence, mathematical reasoning, claims and limitations remain identical throughout the main text and appendices. These limited editorial changes establish no meaningful net difference in overall paper quality.
